run.change_description:
Fixed issue of Datepicker displaying the wrong date for users in UTC+ timezones.

Removed usage of var keyword.  Replaced with const.

Removed .idea/vcs.xml.

Made a shell for the integration test for DatePicker displayed/selected dates.

update tests

summary.intent: Fix bokehjs's DatePicker so the widget's displayed date matches the date it was given, for users in positive-UTC-offset ("UTC+") timezones (bokeh/bokeh#9129), and add an integration test file for the widget.
summary.issue_fit: Met for its stated target: the `_on_select` -> re-render round trip used to show the previous day in positive-UTC-offset zones and now shows the selected day. But the same unconditional offset shift breaks the mirror-image case -- Python-supplied value/min_date/max_date, which arrive as absolute UTC timestamps, not locally-parsed strings -- for negative-UTC-offset browsers; see finding `date_picker/negative-offset-regression`.
summary.coverage: Full merge-base diff read (date_picker.ts, the new integration test file), plus the Python-side date serialization path (bokeh/util/serialization.py, bokeh/core/json_encoder.py, bokeh/models/widgets/inputs.py) that determines what this.model.value/min_date/max_date actually carry in the browser. Selenium/browser execution is unavailable offline; the new test functions were inspected by trace against their fixtures and assertions instead, and the core date-shift logic was independently re-derived and run offline with node across ten IANA timezones (positive, negative, and fractional offsets) at head and merge-base.
check_details: Selenium/browser execution unavailable offline; the new integration test file (tests/integration/widgets/test_datepicker.py) was inspected by trace rather than run.

Reviewer re-derived _unlocal_date in node (TZ env var) at head 36549bca3 across Europe/Paris, America/New_York, Asia/Kolkata, Pacific/Auckland, America/Sao_Paulo, Asia/Kathmandu, Pacific/Chatham, America/St_Johns, Pacific/Kiritimati, and UTC: confirms the fix for the post-selection string round trip and confirms a new one-day-early regression for the Python-timestamp path in every negative-offset zone tested.

findings.title: Skip the offset shift for dates that are already absolute timestamps
findings.trigger: A browser west of UTC (e.g. America/New_York, America/Sao_Paulo) renders a DatePicker whose value, min_date, or max_date came from Python, e.g. `DatePicker(value=datetime.date.today())` -- issue #9129's own repro.
findings.impact: Python encodes those fields as an absolute UTC-midnight timestamp (bokeh/util/serialization.py:184, wired into JSON encoding at bokeh/core/json_encoder.py:186), which `toISOString()` already read correctly pre-fix. The newly added offset subtraction now shifts that instant into the prior UTC day, so the shown date -- and the min/max bounds, which have no other producer -- are one calendar day early.
findings.change: Apply the offset shift only to the locally-parsed string `_on_select` produces; for a value that is already an absolute timestamp, read `getUTCFullYear`/`getUTCMonth`/`getUTCDate` directly instead of shifting and re-reading local `toISOString()`.

observations.fact: test_js_on_change_executes and test_server_on_change_round_trip only distinguish pre-fix from post-fix `_unlocal_date` behavior when the runner's TZ has a nonzero offset; .travis.yml sets no TZ, so under a UTC runner both tests pass identically whether or not the timezone fix (or this regression) is present.
observations.evidence: tests/integration/widgets/test_datepicker.py; .travis.yml has no TZ directive; node repro shows old==new="Fri Sep 20 2019" at TZ=UTC for both the string and numeric-timestamp paths.

requirements.evidence: Re-derived _unlocal_date at head 36549bca3 for the _on_select round-trip path (a locally-parsed toDateString() string): TZ=Europe/Paris and TZ=Asia/Kolkata now render the selected day instead of day-1, matching commit 472e4770d/"Fixed issue of Datepicker displaying the wrong date for users in UTC+ timezones."
